messages:
paul: hey team — long generation getting cut off even though I set timeout on the Python client. using SDK v0.8.2, streaming. anyone seen this? @maria :thinking_face:

maria: hi @paul, can you paste the Client init snippet + how you're calling generate? is this streaming or the regular sync call?

paul: streaming. here's minimal repro:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=\"REDACTED\", timeout=60)  # I set timeout=60s
resp = client.generate(model=\"redwood-large-gen\", prompt=long_prompt, stream=True)
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text)
```
It reliably ends ~15s in with a ReadTimeout error, even when I set REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=120 in env. Happens on my laptop and in our staging service.

li: fwiw, this sounds like httpx/urllib3 semantics biting you. The SDK's `timeout` param can map to a total timeout vs per-socket read/connect time. For streaming the important one is the read timeout — if the server doesn't send a chunk within that window the connection gets cut.

li: try passing an explicit timeout mapping, e.g. `Client(timeout={\"connect\":10, \"read\":300})` or `httpx.Timeout(read=300, connect=10)` depending on how you construct the client. Also check any proxy/load-balancer idle timeouts. ALBs often close at 60s.

paul: repro steps to reproduce quickly:
1) run the snippet above with a prompt that triggers ~1500-3000 tokens generation
2) use stream=True
3) observe cut after ~15s with `ReadTimeout:...`
SDK version: 0.8.2. No fancy proxy in the laptop case.

maria: thanks — filing an internal ticket and pinging eng. Short-term workaround: set a larger read timeout as @li suggested or use non-streaming `client.generate(..., stream=False)` to get whole payload (not ideal). We also have a PR in flight for 0.9.0 that clarifies env var precedence for timeouts. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket SR-8342 created for Paul (paul). Assigned to eng-oncall. Reference: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SR-8342

paul: trying the explicit timeout mapping now, will report back. thanks!
